title: Senior Financial Controller (Xero) — Rebuild & Own the Finance Function of a Fast-Scaling E-commerce Brand
job_title: Senior Financial Controller (Xero) — Rebuild & Own the Finance Function of a Fast-Scaling E-commerce Brand
description: We're an Australian premium e-commerce retailer — pool tables, arcade machines, pinball, kegerators, saunas and more. We do $10M in revenue and we're scaling to $40M over the next two years. We run our own warehousing, national delivery and an installation team. We're ambitious, we move fast, and we are dead serious about fixing our finance function properly this time. We're looking for a Senior Financial Controller to take full ownership of our books, rebuild our Xero from the ground up, and turn it into the system the business actually steers by. This is a long-term, full-time, ongoing role. It is not a project, not a tidy-up, and not a part-time advisory seat. READ THIS BEFORE APPLYING — WE'RE BEING COMPLETELY STRAIGHT WITH YOU Our books are not in good shape, and we're not going to pretend otherwise. Xero is disconnected from our inventory system. Our cost of goods is inflated and nobody can fully explain why. Our chart of accounts can't show us profit by product category or by department. We've had two bookkeepers and two senior finance people through this business and the books are no better than a year ago. We have strong data sitting in our other systems — Shopify, Unleashed, Polar Analytics — but nothing ties together in Xero, and Xero is not currently a source of truth. We are telling you this upfront because we want someone who reads that and gets interested, not nervous. If untangling a genuine mess and building order out of it is the work you're best at and enjoy most, keep reading. If you want a clean set of books to gently maintain, this is the wrong role and we'll both know it quickly. WHAT THIS ROLE ACTUALLY IS You will own the finance function. Not assist it — own it. In your first months the job is heavy reconstruction: you will pull apart what's wrong, rebuild the Xero chart of accounts properly, and rebuild trust in every number. Once it's clean, you run it — month-end, management accounts, cash flow, reporting — and you keep it immaculate. You'll work directly with the CEO and closely with our operations team, and you'll be the person who can answer, with confidence and evidence, “are we actually making money, and where?” WHAT YOU'LL DELIVER The headline outcomes we are hiring you to produce: - Xero rebuilt as the single source of truth — a clean, correctly structured chart of accounts the leadership team trusts without second-guessing. - Profit visibility by product category — pool tables, arcade, pinball, kegerators, dartboards, LED and furniture — so we finally know which categories make money and which don't. This is a build and depends on cost inputs being cleaned up over time; you'll be central to getting there. - Departmental P&L — cost-centre reporting so marketing, sales, operations and admin can each see and own their numbers. - Reliable month-end — a full close and management accounts the business can make real decisions on, every month, on time. - A 13-week rolling cash flow forecast — we have seasonal revenue and financing facilities; we need to see cash coming before it becomes a problem. WHAT YOU'LL OWN DAY TO DAY - Rebuilding and maintaining the Xero chart of accounts and tracking-code structure. - Untangling cost of goods — core stock vs drop-ship, freight-in vs freight-out, installation costs, merchant fees, and the inventory adjustment journals currently muddying the picture. - Owning the reconciliation of data flowing from Shopify and our inventory system (Unleashed) into Xero, with no unexplained variances. Our operations team owns the inventory system itself — you are the person who makes sure it reconciles cleanly into the books. - The full month-end close and management accounts. - The 13-week cash flow view and tracking of our financing facilities. - Bank reconciliation, accounts payable, supplier invoice processing and payment run preparation. - Feeding clean, reliable data to our external Australian tax accountant, who handles tax, GST and BAS. WHO WE'RE LOOKING FOR - This is a senior role and we need a senior person. Specifically: - 6+ years in accounting or finance, with real depth in e-commerce, retail or inventory-heavy businesses. - Genuine Xero mastery — you have personally restructured a chart of accounts and built a tracking-code framework, not just worked inside one someone else set up. Xero certification expected or close to it. - A demonstrable track record of taking messy, untrusted books and making them clean and reliable — this is the single most important thing we're hiring for. - Strong command of inventory and cost-of-goods accounting — you understand how landed cost, stock and COGS move through the books. - Confident building cost-centre and category-level reporting from scratch. - Hands-on with Shopify and an inventory/ERP system (Unleashed or similar). - Self-directed and accountable — you own outcomes, surface problems early, and don't need chasing. - Excellent written and spoken English, and genuinely confident leading a conversation on a weekly video call with the CEO. - A reliable internet connection, a quiet space for video calls, and solid working overlap with Australian Eastern time (AEST). WHAT'S IN IT FOR THE RIGHT PERSON - Full ownership of a finance function from day one — this is your domain to build. - A genuine path to a senior finance leadership seat as we scale toward $40M; we want this person to grow with us. - A long-term, stable, full-time role with a business that's serious about getting this right and will back you to do it. - A proper handover and structured onboarding — you will not be dropped in cold. - Direct line to the CEO; your work will visibly drive how the business makes decisions. - Paid local Philippine public holidays and a genuine commitment to a long-term working relationship. HOW TO APPLY Applications must be submitted through our application form. Applications that come only as a message here, without the form completed, will not be reviewed. Apply here: ---------- We're interviewing immediately and moving quickly for the right person.

title: Sign Industry Estimator
description: **MUST BE AVAILABLE MONDAY THROUGH FRIDAY 8am-4pm MST Position Overview We are a custom sign manufacturing and installation company seeking an experienced Estimator to join our team remotely. In this role, you will read and interpret architectural and shop drawings, develop accurate cost estimates, and build winning bids for interior and exterior sign projects ranging from single-tenant signage to multi-location rollouts. You will work closely with sales, project managers, fabrication, and installation crews to ensure every estimate reflects true scope, true cost, and a margin we can stand behind. The right candidate is detail-obsessed, deadline-driven, and comfortable owning the numbers from takeoff through bid handoff. Key Responsibilities • Read and interpret drawings: Review architectural plans, elevations, site plans, shop drawings, electrical drawings, and landlord/municipal sign criteria packages to define accurate scope. • Perform quantity takeoffs: Extract material types, square footage, linear footage, hardware counts, and electrical specs from drawings and RFP documents. • Build complete estimates: Price materials, fabrication labor, finishing, freight, permitting, engineering, installation labor, equipment (lifts, cranes, traffic control), and applicable markups. • Specify installation scope: Determine mounting methods, wall conditions, electrical requirements, lift or crane needs, permitting obligations, and crew sizing for both interior and exterior installs. • Source and quote vendors: Solicit and evaluate quotes from material suppliers, sub-fabricators, electrical sign manufacturers, permit runners, and installation subcontractors. • Maintain pricing data: Work with Purchasing to ensure material, labor, and burden rates are current • Produce bid documents: Deliver clean, client-ready proposals with clear scope, inclusions, exclusions, assumptions, lead times, and payment terms. • Collaborate cross-functionally: Work with sales on pursuit strategy, with production on buildability, and with project managers on smooth job handoff after award. • Track and analyze: Maintain a bid log, hit-rate tracking, and post-job cost reviews to continuously sharpen estimating accuracy. Required Qualifications • Sign industry experience: 3+ years estimating in custom signage (channel letters, monuments, pylons, wayfinding, ADA, dimensional, vinyl/graphics, and electrical signage). • Drawing literacy: Demonstrated ability to read architectural drawings, shop drawings, electrical schematics, and sign criteria packages without hand-holding. • Pricing fluency: Strong working knowledge of sign materials (aluminum, acrylic, LEDs, power supplies, vinyl, hardware), fabrication processes, finishes, and labor burden. • Installation knowledge: Practical understanding of interior and exterior install methods, wall types, mounting hardware, electrical hookup, lifts, cranes, and permitting workflows. • Excel proficiency: Comfortable with formulas, lookups (VLOOKUP/XLOOKUP/INDEX-MATCH), pivot tables, and conditional logic; able to build and maintain estimating workbooks. • ERP software: Hands-on experience with an ERP or job costing system (e.g., CYRIOUS Control, Shopify Sign, NetSuite, Sage, or similar). Preferred Qualifications • Experience in estimating national rollouts or multi-site programs. • Familiarity with UL listing requirements for electric signs. • Working knowledge of local permitting processes and landlord criteria packages. • Bluebeam, AutoCAD, or other PDF/CAD markup experience. • Background in fabrication, project management, or field installation before moving into estimating. What Success Looks Like in This Role • Estimates are accurate, complete, and submitted on or before deadline. • Bid hit rate improves quarter-over-quarter without margin erosion. • Post-job cost variance stays within target on awarded work. • Sales, production, and installation teams trust the numbers and the scope handoff. description: TITLE: Part-Time Bookkeeper + Cash Flow / Finance Manager (QuickBooks Online) - Remote HOURS: Part-time to start (20-25 hrs/week), with opportunity to grow into full-time Must overlap 2-3 hours with Vancouver, Canada (PST) START: ASAP PAY: Competitive and based on experience. We pay for quality. ABOUT US: We are a Vancouver, Canada-based high-end residential construction supplier and installer (project-based). We work on luxury custom homes and manage large project invoices, deposits, progress payments, and job costs. This is a serious role. We are not looking for a generic VA. We are looking for a real accounting professional who can take ownership of our bookkeeping and help manage the overall financial health of the company. We are looking for someone long-term. If you are looking for short-term work, freelancing, or multiple clients, this role is not a good fit. We want someone who will become part of the company for years, grow with us, and be treated like part of the team. ROLE SUMMARY: You will be responsible for keeping our accounting clean and accurate in QuickBooks Online, ensuring reconciliations are done properly, tracking job profitability, and maintaining cash flow visibility for the owner. Our transaction volume is not huge, but our invoices are large and accuracy is extremely important. RESPONSIBILITIES: QuickBooks Online bookkeeping and cleanup. Bank and credit card reconciliations. Accounts payable and accounts receivable. Transaction categorization and proper coding. Maintaining a clean chart of accounts and organized records. Tracking income and costs by job/project (job costing). Tracking deposits and progress payments correctly. Monitoring job profitability while projects are active. Maintaining a cash flow statement and identifying cash flow risks early. Providing a simple monthly financial health summary to the owner. Monthly reporting including Profit and Loss, Balance Sheet, AR Aging, cash summary, and basic job margin snapshot. Preparing clean year-end records for our external accountant. Supporting GST/PST preparation (Canada). Guidance will be provided. REQUIREMENTS (STRICT): Strong QuickBooks Online experience. Strong reconciliation skills. Month-end close experience. Experience preparing financial reports. Strong English communication (written and spoken). High attention to detail and strong follow-through. Professionalism and confidentiality. PREFERRED (STRONGLY): Construction or project-based accounting experience. Job costing experience. Audit, controller, or accounting manager experience. Buildertrend or similar software experience BENEFITS: Long-term stable role. Part-time to start with growth to full-time. Two weeks paid vacation per year (once full-time). Respectful, professional working environment. Clear expectations and communication. IMPORTANT: HOW TO APPLY (READ CAREFULLY) Applications that do not follow instructions will be ignored. We are using this process to filter applicants who are serious and detail-oriented. STEP 1: Write this at the top of your application: I READ THE INSTRUCTIONS STEP 2: Answer these questions in writing: Explain step-by-step how you reconcile a bank account in QuickBooks Online. Explain your month-end close process in checklist style. Video can be Loom, Google Drive, or YouTube unlisted. OPTIONAL BONUS: Attach a screenshot of a bank reconciliation screen you personally completed in QuickBooks Online. Blur all confidential information. FINAL NOTE: If your profile includes unrelated services such as social media, graphic design, video editing, or lead generation, we will assume accounting is not your main skill. We are looking for an accounting professional who takes this role seriously.

title: Shopify E-Commerce Finance Controller — P&L, ROAS & Cashflow for a 12-Store Dropshipping Group
job_title: Shopify E-Commerce Finance Controller — P&L, ROAS & Cashflow for a 12-Store Dropshipping Group
description: Summary Shopify E-Commerce Finance Controller — Daily Store P&L, ROAS & Cashflow Reconciliation for a 12-Store Dropshipping Group (Proactive, Self-Directing) Intro We run a portfolio of around 12 Shopify dropshipping stores across two entities (Netherlands and US), scaling toward roughly €25M this year. We need someone who lives and breathes Shopify store economics — daily revenue, COGS, ad spend, ROAS, payment fees and refunds — and who can make every store's P&L tie out to the actual cash landing in our accounts. If you have run the numbers behind Shopify dropshipping stores before, this will feel familiar. If you have only done traditional bookkeeping, it will not. About us We operate a growing portfolio of Shopify dropshipping stores in fashion and home décor. We launch, scale and sell individual stores, so each one is run as a standalone business unit with its own daily P&L — and each one has to stay sale-ready, meaning a buyer can review clean store-level financials at any ---------- nt. Quiet months run €400K–500K; Black Friday peaks hit €1M–2M. We buy traffic primarily through Google Ads (and Pinterest on some stores), fulfil through a 3PL partner, and run a multi-provider payment stack. What you'll do Own the daily P&L for each Shopify store — either filling it directly or coordinating the tea ---------- mber(s) who do, while owning the accuracy either way. Each daily row tracks: Revenue, COGS, Google Adspend, Mediabuying fee, transaction/payment provider fee, refunds, and the resulting Profit, ROAS, Profit %, COGS % and CVR % Pull supplier and fulfilment invoices from Slack daily and book accurate COGS per store (product + shipping + fulfilment, often combined on one invoice) Reconcile daily ad spend pulled from the Google Ads and Pinterest accounts against what is logged in each store P&L, and against Shopify revenue and order counts Track real payment provider fees and payout timing across Shopify Payments, multiple PayPal accounts, PayPal Hong Kong, WOP Payments, Ocean Payments and Airwallex — not estimates Catch the leaks that distort dropshipping P&Ls: refunds processed through old/disconnected PayPal accounts, chargebacks and dispute fees, FX conversion costs (EUR/USD/HKD), and payout delays — and make the internal P&L reconcile to actual bank cash Build and own weekly, monthly and quarterly reporting per store and per entity Evolve our current daily P&L template into a complete, sale-ready store-level reporting standard Coordinate the existing operational finance team (payments processing and invoice control) What we're looking for Hands-on experience running or controlling the financials of Shopify (or comparable DTC) e-commerce stores — this is a hard requirement You understand store-level unit economics: ROAS, AOV, CVR, COGS %, blended margin, and how ad spend, refunds and payment fees move the real profit number Comfortable pulling and reconciling data from Shopify, Google Ads, and multiple payment providers in multiple currencies Strong reconciliation discipline — you know why reported profit and bank cash diverge in an e-commerce business, and how to close the gap Reliable async communicator inside a remote international team Nice to have Dropshipping / 3PL fulfilment invoicing experience Experience preparing store-level financials for a sale or due diligence (we sell stores) Yuki (NL) and/or Xero (US) experience Experience automating Shopify/ad-account/payment-provider data into reporting The mindset that matters most We have worked with bookkeepers who fill cells correctly and stop there. That is not enough for a fast-moving store portfolio. We want someone who notices a store's COGS % drifting and digs into why, who spots a refund leak through an old PayPal account before it eats a month of margin, and who proposes and builds improvements to the reporting system on their own initiative. You should be the person who makes the numbers trustworthy without being asked twice. How to apply Start your application with the word RECONCILED so we know you read the full post. Then answer briefly: Which Shopify or DTC stores' financials have you run or controlled? Give revenue scale and your exact role. Walk us through how you would find and close a gap between a store's reported P&L profit and the actual cash in the bank. Would you prefer to do the daily store P&L hands-on, coordinate a team that does it, or both — and why?

title: Senior US Tax Reviewer (UltraTax/CCH) — Full-Time
description: About Whyte CPA P.C. We're a virtual CPA firm in Gilbert, Arizona serving about 60 monthly clients. Our niche is S-corporation owners and real estate investors. Small firm, lean operation, high standards on the work that goes out the door. The owner currently does all final review and signs every return. That bottleneck is why this role exists. We need a senior reviewer who hits the ground running and produces output clean enough that the owner's final pass is a 10-minute confirmation, not real review work. What You'll Actually Do This is a year-round, full-time, review-first role. Here's what you'll spend your time on: Tax return review. Federal and state returns prepared by staff. Heavy on 1040s with K-1s, 1120Ss, partnerships, and 1041s. Most returns include K-1s coming in (most prepared by us), Schedule E with rentals, brokerage statements, and frequently a Schedule C or Schedule E pg 1. These are not generic 1040s. You catch errors, identify missed positions, flag judgment calls, and write clear review notes back to the preparer. Bookkeeping review (monthly). QBO books prepared by staff each month. You don't do bookkeeping — but you must be able to review it at a senior level. You identify reconciliation issues, miscoded transactions, and items affecting tax planning before the books feed into planning workups. Quarterly tax planning review. Staff prepares projections in UltraTax's tax planner using annualized financials. You review for accuracy, identify missed strategies, and flag unreasonable assumptions before the work reaches the owner and client. You may also handle some planning prep directly on the most complex clients, or step in when staff bandwidth is tight. IRS and state tax authority correspondence. Notice review, research, and drafting responses. Volume is low (a few per month). Routine notices (math errors, balance due, missing forms) you handle end-to-end. Complex resolution work (payment plans, penalty abatement, audits, OICs, appeals) is collaborative — you bring the research and reasoning, we work through the approach together, owner reviews and signs. We don't expect deep OIC or appeals experience on day one. We expect a strong thinker who can learn the procedures. Owner holds representation authority before the IRS; EA credential is a plus but not required. IRS Solutions Software is used for transcripts and case management. Complex return prep. Most prep work is handled by staff. You'll prepare returns yourself when they require senior-level judgment from prep through completion, or when staff bandwidth is tight. This is not the bulk of your time, but it will happen, and we want someone who treats it as part of the role rather than an exception. New service lines we may build together. We're exploring bringing cost segregation studies in-house and may add other advisory work over time. We're not looking for someone who has done it all before — we're looking for someone who can think critically, learn alongside us, and bring solutions rather than problems. Who You Are You have 5–7 years of US tax experience, with 2–3 years specifically in a review capacity — not just preparation. Be ready to talk about the difference. A preparer who started reviewing six months ago is not what we're looking for. A preparer for three years who has been reviewing for three years is. You have hands-on experience with UltraTax CS, CCH Axcess, Lacerte, or ProConnect. You know S-corp work concretely: basis tracking, §199A computation, reasonable comp analysis, distributions vs. wages. Partnership review experience is a strong plus. You write in clear, professional English (C1 or C2). Review notes need to be actionable for the preparer. Client communications need to land cleanly with US clients. You are detail-oriented and self-policing. When you don't know something, you say so and look it up rather than guessing. You flag your own uncertainty before someone has to ask. You are comfortable with AI-augmented workflows. Our review process uses Claude and TaxGPT alongside human judgment. The AI workflow is firm standard, not optional. Strong candidates are either already using AI tools in their work or genuinely curious to learn. Candidates who view AI as a gimmick or want to skip it on "easy" returns are not a fit. You are self-directed in a remote-first environment. The owner travels for portions of the year and your time zone overlap will shift accordingly. We need someone who can run the review function with minimal oversight, not someone who needs daily check-ins to stay on track. Real estate experience (rentals, short-term rentals, cost segregation, 1031 exchanges) is helpful but not required. We can teach the niche; we can't teach review judgment. Software Stack Required: UltraTax CS (preferred) or CCH Axcess, TaxDome, QuickBooks Online Acceptable in place of UltraTax: Lacerte or ProConnect with willingness to learn UltraTax Not acceptable: Drake-only experience Used in workflow: Claude Pro, TaxGPT (Agent Andrew), IRS Solutions, Excel, Adobe Acrobat Pro If your tax software experience is Drake only, please don't apply. We're not the right fit. Compensation Detail Base salary: $3,800/month USD (paid twice monthly via Wise, on time, every time) 13th month: $3,800 paid in December, prorated for partial first year Internet stipend: $50/month Total annual comp: $50,000 USD Hours: Full-time. Compensation is salary — you are not paid hourly or for overtime. The expectation is that work gets done at high quality. During tax season (Feb 1–April 15), expect 50–55 hour weeks. In off-season, you manage your own time as long as work is current and communication is maintained. Tax season support: One long weekend (Friday–Sunday) off during tax season, scheduled with two weeks notice, to maintain consistent quality. Philippine holidays: All standard PH public holidays observed and paid. No work expected. Off-season flexibility: Take time when work is slow. We don't track formal PTO. Work gets done, communication is maintained, time is yours to manage. Negotiation: Base may be increased to $4,000/month for an exceptional candidate after the test process. Hiring Process 1. Application — Submit per the instructions below. Generic applications are discarded immediately. 2. First screen — 30-minute video call with the owner. 3. Paid test return — One real return (sanitized client data), $400 USD, ~3–4 hours of your time, due within 7 days. You produce review notes in your own format using your own workflow. We're testing your judgment, not your ability to follow our SOP. 4. Judgment interview — 30-minute call discussing your test return, plus 2–3 scenario questions about how you'd handle specific review situations. 5. Reference check — One reference from a recent supervisor or peer reviewer who can speak to your work. 6. Offer Total process: 2–3 weeks for serious candidates. How to Apply Send your application with the subject line: "Senior Reviewer — [Your Full Name]" Include the following in the body. If your application doesn't follow this structure, we'll assume you didn't read the post and won't respond. 1. Experience summary (3–5 sentences): Your years in US tax, your years specifically in a review capacity, the type of firm you've worked at (US firm, mid-tier PH outsourcing operation, etc.), and the volume/type of returns you've reviewed. 2. Tax software: Which of UltraTax CS, CCH Axcess, Lacerte, ProConnect have you used? For each, name the specific modules (1040, 1120S, 1065, 1041) and roughly how many returns you've worked in each. 3. DISC scores (if available). If you haven't taken DISC, OnlineJobs.ph has a free 10-minute test — please take it before applying. 4. A specific review catch you're proud of (2–3 sentences): What was the issue, how did you find it, what was the correction, what would have happened if it shipped uncaught. Specific and technical, not abstract. 5. AI in your workflow (2–3 sentences): How do you currently use Claude, ChatGPT, or other AI tools in your tax work? If you don't currently use them, how would you approach learning a firm's AI-augmented review process? 6. Availability: Earliest start date and any current employment that would need to transition. We're hiring for fit, not speed. Process moves quickly for serious applicants — but we'll wait for the right person. What This Role Is Not — Not part-time or seasonal — Not for someone learning US tax (you should already know it) — Not a stepping stone to bigger firms — we want someone who wants to settle in We're looking forward to hearing from you.

description: A B2B store buildout partner delivering complete retail store projects across Canada and the USA — fixtures, refrigeration, walk-ins, millwork, racking, and kitchen equipment, coordinated through one accountable team. Primary clients are grocery chains, pharmacies, hardware stores, and specialty retailers opening or expanding locations. This is a full-time, fully remote position, starting on the estimating team. You will build detailed cost estimates for retail store fixture projects — primarily gondola shelving and related store equipment. Each estimate starts from a customer's specifications and a store layout, and ends as a structured, spec-accurate quote ready for review. Day to day, that means reading layouts and specifications, performing component-level takeoffs and dimensional math, retrieving cost pricing from manufacturer tools, applying per-project pricing formulas, and assembling the estimate in QuickBooks Online. You will flag missing information, request pricing from manufacturers where needed, and submit completed estimates for approval before they reach the customer. Estimating happens within defined product systems and manufacturer pricing — the focus is accuracy and discipline, not invention. The role also sits alongside project coordination: tracking quotes through revision and approval, keeping specifications consistent, and coordinating with the sales lead and manufacturing partners. It reports to a senior tea ---------- mber and has a clear path toward broader project responsibility for the right person. WHO WE ARE LOOKING FOR The trait that separates a strong estimator from an average one is accuracy under detail. A single wrong dimension or missed component flows straight into a quote and costs real money. We are looking for someone who treats spec accuracy as non-negotiable — who does the math twice, catches the gap before it ships, and flags an unknown instead of guessing it. We also want someone who communicates with discipline — clear, direct, and proactive about surfacing problems early. Candidates without real, hands-on estimating experience will not be considered. REQUIREMENTS 1. Several years of hands-on cost estimating and quantity takeoff — reading drawings or layouts and translating them into priced, structured estimates. Background in construction, millwork, casework, or retail fixtures. Estimating limited to manufacturing unit costing or bill-of-materials work, with no takeoff from drawings, is not a fit for this role. 2. Strong dimensional and mathematical accuracy — comfort with component-level math, including depths, section counts, and run breakdowns, and the habit of checking work before it moves forward. 3. CAD literacy — able to read architectural floor plans and shop drawings. Experience with AutoCAD, SketchUp, or similar is expected. 4. Clear written English and disciplined communication — someone who flags assumptions and gaps rather than guessing, and coordinates cleanly across sales, manufacturers, and project staff. 5. Experience coordinating projects, schedules, or vendors alongside estimating work is a strong advantage. An engineering background — civil, structural, or architectural — is also a strong advantage. HIRING PROCESS 1. Application review — form responses and resume are reviewed first. 2. A short interview — roughly 15 minutes, booked online 3. Second interview —around 30 minutes. 4.  Offer — extended to the candidate who passes all three stages. TO APPLY All applications are submitted through one form. Applications sent any other way may not be reviewed. ---------- The form takes a few minutes and covers your experience, software, availability, and rate. Have your resume ready to upload.

Your experience in financial analysis (cash flow modeling, P&L management, budgeting, and forecasting) for an ecommerce AND DTC brands? 2. description: Remote Landscape Estimator & Designer — Full-Time, Exclusive Company: Skyline Exteriors is a fast-growing landscaping design and build company based in Skokie, Illinois, serving Chicago’s north side and northwest suburbs. We work with high-end residential clients, commercial properties, HOAs, and municipalities. We are targeting $10M in revenue this year and building a world-class remote operations team to get there. What You Will Do You will own the estimating and design function end-to-end. This is not a support role — you will be the person responsible for producing accurate, professional, and margin-protected estimates and landscape design plans that win jobs and protect our profitability. Your core responsibilities are as follows. You will receive client scope information from our appointment setters and account managers, then produce detailed cost estimates for landscaping design and build projects — including materials, labor hours, plant selections, and hardscape elements. You will create 2D and 3D landscape design renderings using tools such as SketchUp, AutoCAD, Vectorworks, DynaScape, or equivalent. You will select plants appropriate for the Illinois climate and USDA Hardiness Zone 5b/6a, with knowledge of native species, seasonal interest, soil requirements, and maintenance profiles. You will ensure every quote maintains a gross margin of at least 50% and a labor variance within 5% of actual. You will track revision counts and aim to close quotes within two revisions.  You will flag any scope gaps or under-scoped items before a quote is submitted. You will participate in weekly review calls with our estimator and GM. Performance Standards (Tracked in Our Operating System) These are the exact KPIs you will be measured against from Day 1: KPI Target: Gross Margin per Quote ? 50% Labor Variance (estimated vs. actual) ? 5% Under-Scope Rate ? 2% Average Revision Count per Quote ? 2 Rework Rate (jobs requiring re-do) ? 3% What We Are Looking For 1. Education and Background. You are a licensed architect, civil engineer, landscape architect, or have a degree in horticulture, environmental design, or a related field. You have at least 2 years of hands-on experience producing estimates and design plans for landscaping or exterior construction projects. Experience with US-based clients — especially Midwest or Illinois — is a strong advantage. 2. Technical Skills. You are proficient in at least one professional design tool (SketchUp, AutoCAD, Vectorworks, DynaScape, or similar). You can produce clean, client-presentable 2D plans and 3D renderings. You know how to build a line-item estimate with material costs, labor hours, and markup. You are comfortable working in Google Sheets, Excel, or a CRM-based estimating tool. 3. Horticulture Knowledge. You understand plant selection for USDA Zone 5b/6a (Chicago area). You know which plants thrive in Illinois winters, which are native, and how to specify them correctly in a design. You can recommend plant palettes that are both visually compelling and low-maintenance for upmarket residential clients. 4. Remote Work Capability. You have a reliable internet connection of at least 20 Mbps. You have a dedicated, quiet workspace. You are available during US Central Time business hours (8 AM – 5 PM CST), Monday through Friday. You have a backup power and internet solution. You are responsive on Slack and email within 15 minutes during work hours. 5. Commitment. This is a full-time, exclusive position. You will not take on other clients or freelance work while employed with Skyline. We are building a long-term team and expect the same commitment in return. What We Offer - Full-time remote position with stable, long-term employment - Competitive salary based on experience (state your expected rate in your application) - Direct access to our GM and operations team — no bureaucracy - Clear KPI-based performance reviews with raise eligibility tied to results - Work on real, high-value projects ( 500K+ residential and commercial installs - A company that is scaling fast and rewards people who perform How to Apply: Send the following to be considered. Applications without all four items will not be reviewed. 1. Your updated resume or CV 2. A portfolio of at least 3 landscape design projects you personally worked on (PDF or link) 3. A sample estimate or cost breakdown you produced (can be anonymized) 4. A 2–3 sentence answer to this question: “A client wants a full backyard redesign in Naperville, IL. What are the first three plants you would consider specifying and why?” Subject line: “Landscape Estimator + Designer — [Your Name]”

You will build genuine rapport, map full family trees, uncover pain points, and persistently contact every necessary heir/sibling/co-owner — even if the first person says “no” — to gather information for affidavits of heirship and secure sign-overs or majority interest. job_title: Part-Time Xero Bookkeeper (UK Short-Term Rental / Airbnb Business)
description: We are a UK serviced accommodation (short-term rental) company running around 13 properties across Brighton, Watford and Leicester, and we are still growing. We need a reliable, detail-focused bookkeeper to own the day-to-day books in Xero. This is not general bookkeeping. Different properties run on different ownership models: management agreements for investor-owned units, a joint venture, and rent-to-rent units we run on our own account. Money that belongs to property owners and JV partners must be kept completely separate from our own company income. If you have done the books for a short-term rental, Airbnb management or property management business before, you will recognise this setup straight away. WHAT YOU WILL DO - Reconcile bank transactions across all our accounts in Xero, weekly rather than only at month-end. - Code income and costs to the correct investor control accounts (the 880 series), or to our own company accounts where it is genuinely our income or cost, applying property and type tracking to every line. - Match payouts from Airbnb, ---------- , Vrbo, Stripe, PayPal and direct bookings to the right bookings and properties, including single Stripe payouts that cover several bookings across more than one property. - Split our joint-venture transactions to the agreed shares (for example 60/40, and 50/50 for dates before a split change). - Process director's loan entries, supplier bills and client invoices. - Produce monthly owner statements for each investor property, plus the partner statement for our Watford joint venture. - Keep a running query log for anything you cannot confidently identify. - Support year-end and our UK accountant at reporting time. HOW THIS ROLE WORKS (please read carefully) - You work independently. You log in and do the work on your own schedule. You do not need me online to work, and I will not be supervising live. I need someone confident working autonomously. - Month-end is tied to our payment date. Property owners are paid on the 1st of each month, so the monthly close and all owner statements must be finished by the last working day of the month. This is the single most important deadline in the role and it does not move. - Fixed weekly hours. I need someone who commits to set hours each week (15 to 20 hours total) at agreed times, with at least a few hours of overlap with the UK working day. This is not a fit-it-in-when-you-can arrangement. - Communication. Post questions in our shared channel and I will respond within 24 hours. Tasks I send should be actioned within 48 hours. If you cannot hit a deadline, tell me in advance. SYSTEMS WE USE Xero (core), Uplisting (channel manager and PMS), Stripe (several connected accounts), Airbnb, ---------- , Vrbo and PayPal. Receipts come in by email and photo and are matched to card spend. We are not VAT registered, so understanding why gross booking income flows through control accounts rather than through our own turnover is important. REQUIREMENTS - 3+ years Xero experience, certification preferred. - Experience with UK clients (GBP, UK bookkeeping conventions). - Property management, short-term rental or Airbnb management bookkeeping experience strongly preferred. - Comfortable with control accounts, owner statements, and OTA and Stripe reconciliation. - Disciplined about flagging and querying anything you cannot confidently identify, rather than guessing. - Able to work fully independently with minimal supervision. - Reliable, with consistent weekly availability and UK daytime overlap. - Strong written English and responsive communication. TO APPLY 1. Start your message with the word RECONCILE so I know you read this post in full. 2. Send your CV. 3. Record a short Loom video (about 2 minutes) explaining your Xero and property or short-term-rental experience. 4. Answer this: an Airbnb payout of 4,200 pounds lands in the bank covering five separate bookings across three different properties, each owned by a different investor. Walk me through, step by step, how you would reconcile that in Xero so that each owner's account ends up correct. Applications that skip the keyword, the video or the question will not be considered.

title: Financial Controller
description: Ikigai Cases is hiring a Controller! Location: Remote / Work From Home Reports to: CEO About the Company Ikigai Cases ( ---------- ) is a fast-growing ecommerce brand manufacturing aerospace-grade aluminum pill cases. Founded in December 2021 by two brothers after their father’s neurological diagnosis led them to discovering the issues with plastic pill organizers, we’ve built a multi-million dollar business in just over four years with a team of 25 across the globe. Our mission is simple: make exceptional pill cases and provide exceptional customer service. We deliver on this by managing in-house fulfillment at our Washington, DC facility (including custom engraving) and maintaining obsessive attention to detail. About the Role We are hiring a Controller to take complete ownership of our financial operations - accounting, reporting, payroll, budgeting, cash flow, tax coordination, and financial systems. This is a critical senior role, and we’re looking for someone whose professional identity is built around three things: the integrity of the numbers, running the finance function end-to-end, and providing strategic financial insight to the CEO. The ideal candidate has served as a Controller (or equivalent) for an e-commerce or DTC brand in the $10–30M revenue range. You understand the financial rhythms of e-commerce: Shopify revenue recognition, inventory accounting, seasonal cash flow swings, sales tax across multiple states, and the speed at which decisions need to be made. If you’ve done this before at a similar-sized company, you already know what we need. At $11.5M in revenue and targeting $30M by 2028, our financial complexity is outpacing our financial infrastructure. We need someone who builds systems, not just operates inside them. You’ll report directly to the CEO and work hand-in-hand with our external financial advisor. No layers of management between you and the decisions your work supports. Core Responsibilities Monthly Close & Financial Reporting: Close books by the 10th of every month. Produce reviewed P&L, balance sheet, and cash flow statements in Finaloop. Resolve misclassifications proactively. Maintain a clean chart of accounts. No CEO intervention required. Budgeting & Financial Planning: Prepare and maintain monthly, quarterly, and annual budgets. Own budget vs. actuals: produce variance reports monthly alongside the P&L close with plain-language explanations. Update balance sheet items and expenses weekly inside the company’s financial models. Cash Flow Management & Forecasting: Maintain the 13-week cash flow forecast weekly and proactively. Flag upcoming cash movements, exposure, and risks before they become surprises. This is one of the most critical tools the CEO uses for capital allocation. Payroll Operations (Zero-Error Standard): Own bi-weekly payroll across ADP (US) and Deel (Philippines). Submit the morning of payroll day, every cycle. PTO, overtime, and deductions captured before submission. You catch discrepancies before they reach the CEO. Tax Coordination & Compliance: Own the relationship with Numeral on multi-state sales tax filings. Maintain the estimated tax payment tracker. Coordinate with our external CPA on annual filings. Flag tax exposure and timing proactively. Vendor Payments, Disbursements & Financial Systems: Execute and double-check all vendor payments (Venmo, PayPal, wire). Track owner distributions and related-party transactions. Manage Finaloop, Shopify revenue reconciliation, and Google Sheets financial modeling. Manage financial admin including insurance, vendor accounts, and benefits. CEO Reporting & Ad Hoc Analysis: Weekly: 13WCF update, flagged variances, upcoming cash movements. Monthly: clean financial statements with brief narrative. As needed: ad hoc financial analysis without requiring a detailed spec. Why You Should Take This Role -You’ll work at a brand obsessed with its customers, with a loyal following. Read the reviews: ---------- /pages/reviews -A company that’s scaled rapidly in 4 years and is aggressively investing in growth. -You’ll work hand-in-hand with the founder, not through layers of management, with full autonomy to own your domain. -The company was founded to solve a personal problem - Tavish’s father battled a neurological condition for a decade and the family discovered the issues with plastic pill organizers. -You’ll own the entire financial function for a company on a trajectory from $11.5M to $30M - a career-defining role for the right person. Required Experience & Skills -5+ years in accounting, bookkeeping, or finance operations -Prior Controller or senior finance role at a company doing $10M+ in annual revenue - you’ve owned the full financial function, not just pieces of it -E-commerce or DTC company experience strongly preferred - Shopify revenue recognition, inventory accounting, seasonal cash flow, multi-state sales tax -Experience closing books independently, on a monthly cadence, without supervision -Demonstrated accuracy record - you should be able to speak to this specifically -US GAAP familiarity (CPA not required, but you must understand the principles) -Experience preparing monthly, quarterly, and annual budgets -Payroll experience across multiple platforms -Advanced Google Sheets / Excel (SUMIFS, financial modeling, pivot tables) -Strong proficiency with Finaloop, QuickBooks Online, or equivalent cloud accounting platform -Strong written and verbal English; ability to explain financial insights to non-financial stakeholders Nice-to-Have Experience -Experience working remotely for a US-based company from the Philippines -Exposure to sales tax compliance across multiple US states -Experience using Notion (or similar task management software) -EOS (Entrepreneurial Operating System) familiarity -Prior experience coordinating with external CPAs and tax advisors What We’re Really Looking For -Technical skills get you in the door. These traits determine whether you succeed: -Detail orientation as professional pride - you catch your own errors before they go out, and you change your process so they don’t recur. -Proactive disclosure - you surface problems before being asked, even when it’s uncomfortable. -Ownership without supervision - if it’s due, it’s done. No prompting required. -Direct communication - you push back when something doesn’t look right. -Reliability - when you say you’ll be available, you’re available. When you can’t be, you say so immediately. Compensation Details & Schedule -Compensation: TBD based on candidate experience. Target compensation will be requested during screening. -Work Hours: 50 hours/week, Monday–Friday. Core overlap with US Eastern hours (9AM–5PM EST). -Paid Holidays: 10 paid holidays per year -PTO: 1 week earned for every 6 months worked at the company -Location: Remote / Work From Home To Apply Fill out the application form here: ---------- /jobs/6f92864d-dc4d-41bc ---------- f7bcfcf498e This application includes a number of questions in order to ensure we hire an outstanding candidate for this position, so please be advised in advance that it will take time to complete. Applications are reviewed on a rolling basis. Qualified candidates will be contacted for interviews. Applications on OnlineJobs.ph, DMs, and messages sent via email will not be reviewed.

description: Bookkeeper – Airbnb & Property Management Clients Essential Attributes We are looking for someone with: Experience working with Airbnb management companies, letting agents, property businesses, or other client money businesses At least 3 years of UK bookkeeping experience Minimum of 3 years’ experience using Xero and Hubdoc Strong understanding of VAT Excellent written and verbal communication skills Strong time management skills and the ability to meet deadlines Excellent organisation and attention to detail Ability to work independently in a remote environment Reliable internet connection and a suitable home office setup To be considered for the role, you must submit: A personalised message explaining your experience with Airbnb management businesses, letting agents, or property management clients A short video introducing yourself Your availability for an interview over the next 7 days Please use the following subject/title when submitting your application: [Your Name] | Airbnb Bookkeeper Summary LJY Accountants is a growing accountancy practice specialising in property, landlord, and investment-focused clients. We are looking for a proactive, detail-oriented bookkeeper to join our team and support a portfolio of UK-based clients, with a particular focus on Airbnb and short-term rental management businesses. These clients often operate an agency-style model, involving client money, owner balances, multiple properties, and detailed monthly reporting. You will work closely with the UK-based team and report directly to management. This role is not client-facing, but strong communication with the internal team is essential. The ideal candidate will have strong technical bookkeeping knowledge, particularly around VAT, client money, property income, Airbnb payouts, and accurate cost allocation by property. Key Responsibilities General Bookkeeping Carry out general bookkeeping duties for a portfolio of clients Maintain accurate and up-to-date accounting records Take responsibility for your own portfolio of bookkeeping work Review your own work before submission Work with colleagues where queries or issues arise Report key financial information to management Support ad hoc reporting and finance projects where required Airbnb and Property Management Clients Correctly post and reconcile Airbnb payouts Understand and apply agent vs principal accounting treatment Record management fees as revenue Record owner balances and funds held on behalf of landlords as client money liabilities Maintain and reconcile client money accounts Help prepare monthly owner statements where required Allocate income and costs by individual property using Xero tracking categories or equivalent systems Allocate shared or bulk costs, such as software, supplies, cleaning, or maintenance, consistently across properties VAT and Compliance Prepare and review VAT returns Apply the correct VAT treatment to management fees Apply reverse charge VAT correctly on Airbnb service fees Ensure correct VAT coding for cleaning, maintenance, software, repairs, and property-related costs Flag VAT or compliance issues to management where needed Software and Systems You must be confident using: Xero on a daily basis Hubdoc for invoice and receipt processing Xero bank reconciliation Tracking categories or property-level reporting Digital bookkeeping workflows Advanced Hubdoc responsibilities will include: Processing high volumes of invoices and receipts Applying the correct VAT codes Assigning tracking categories or properties at the point of entry Reviewing source documents for accuracy Querying unclear or incomplete documents with the internal team Experience with property management systems such as Guesty, Hostfully, Hospitable, or similar platforms would be useful, but is not essential. You should be comfortable reconciling property management system data to Xero, bank transactions, Airbnb payouts, and owner balances. Additional Responsibilities Preferred but not essential Experience with any of the following would be beneficial: Initial preparation of monthly payroll journals Initial preparation of basic annual accounts Initial preparation of self-assessment tax return information Preparation and submission of confirmation statements Working with landlord, property investor, or serviced accommodation clients About the Role This is a remote bookkeeping role within a growing UK accountancy practice. You will be expected to manage deadlines, communicate clearly with the team, and maintain accurate records across multiple clients. We are looking for someone who is reliable, organised, technically strong, and comfortable taking ownership of their work. This role would suit someone who has previous experience working with accountancy practices, Airbnb management companies, letting agents, or property-focused businesses.

title: Senior US Tax Accountant
description: ABOUT SAGA Saga Accounting Solutions is a US-based accounting and tax firm serving small business owners, with a growing focus on landscaping companies across the United States. We provide bookkeeping, tax preparation, and advisory services. We are a small, high-performing team that values accuracy, ownership, and clear communication. ROLE SUMMARY We’re looking for a full-time Philippines-based Senior US Tax Accountant to help prepare and perform first-pass reviews of US individual and business tax returns. Work hours are flexible with 3 hour daily overlap hours required. Your main outcome: Accurately prepare and conduct initial review of tax returns to reduce the owner's review time per return. You will work on US clients only, coordinating closely with the owner (an Enrolled Agent). KEY RESPONSIBILITIES 1) Prepare and perform first-pass review of US tax returns: - Individuals: Form 1040 (including Schedule C, Schedule E where applicable) - Businesses: Primarily Form 1065 and 1120S, some 1120 2) Build clear, organized workpapers for each engagement: - Tie-outs to trial balances for entity returns - Supporting schedules (depreciation, loans, equity/basis, etc.) 3) Identify missing information and prepare concise question lists for the owner / client. 4) Draft responses to IRS and state notices following firm templates and guidance (owner will finalize). 5) Follow firm checklists and SOPs to ensure consistent quality and reduce review time. 6) Maintain accurate status updates and time tracking for all assigned returns. 7) Communicate proactively with the team via email /Slack and our practice management system. QUALIFICATIONS Required: - Minimum 3 years recent experience preparing US tax returns in a public accounting or BPO setting. - Hands-on experience with Individual returns (Form 1040 + common schedules) and Entity returns (Form 1065 and/or 1120S) - Proficient with QBO - Experience with at least one major US tax software (Drake Tax and CCH Axcess are a plus). - Strong written English; able to draft clear internal notes and client-facing email drafts. - High attention to detail and ability to follow checklists and procedures. - Stable internet connection and ability to work with overlap in US business hours (at least 3 hours per day). NICE TO HAVE: -Experience with US small businesses in trades/contracting/landscaping or similar industries. -Prior work for a fully virtual US accounting / tax firm. WHAT WE OFFER - Competitive salary in PHP based on experience (to be discussed). - Fully remote role with a small, collaborative team. - Direct mentorship from a US Enrolled Agent. - Opportunity for stable, long-term employment and increased responsibility over time. WORK SCHEDULE & TOOLS - Full-time, remote. - Required overlap with US business hours (e.g., late afternoon/evening PH time). - We primarily use: QuickBooks Online, Drake Tax, Tallyfor, Google Workspace, and Financial Cents Practice Management System. HOW TO APPLY Please submit the following (in English): 1) Your CV/resume. 2) A short cover letter answering: 3) How many US returns did you personally prepare last tax season (break down 1040 / 1065 / 1120S / 1120)? 4) Which tax software have you used, and for how many seasons? 5) Describe the typical US clients you’ve worked with (industry, size, entity types). title: Senior US Tax Preparer (UltraTax) - Full-Time
description: ABOUT WHYTE CPA P.C. We're a virtual CPA firm in Gilbert, Arizona serving about 60 monthly clients. Our niche is S-corporation owners and real estate investors. Small firm, lean operation, high standards on the work that goes out the door. The owner does all final review and signs every return. He's not trying to hand that off right now — he's trying to stop spending it on cleanup. Right now too much review time goes to fixing prep that should have come in clean. This role exists to fix that. We need a senior preparer whose work product is clean, complete, and well-reasoned enough that the owner's review is fast confirmation, not rework. If you're the kind of preparer who hands up tidy workpapers, flags your own open questions before anyone asks, and never guesses when you could check — read on. WHAT YOU'LL ACTUALLY DO This is a year-round, full-time, prep-first role. COMPLEX RETURN PREPARATION. Federal and state returns: heavy on 1040s with K-1s, 1120Ss, partnerships, and 1041s. Most returns include K-1s (most prepared by us), Schedule E with rentals, brokerage statements, and frequently a Schedule C or Schedule E pg 1. These are not generic 1040s. You prepare the returns that require senior-level judgment — S-corp basis, Section 199A, depreciation, multistate — from source documents through clean, review-ready work product. QUARTERLY TAX PLANNING PREP. Using UltraTax's tax planner and annualized financials, you build the projection, identify planning opportunities, and flag unreasonable assumptions for the owner's review. IRS AND STATE NOTICE WORK (LATER). Low volume, a few a month. You won't own this on day one — but as you settle in, routine notices (math errors, balance due, missing forms) become work you draft and handle, with the owner reviewing and signing. WHAT THIS ROLE DOES NOT INCLUDE: bookkeeping (a teammate owns that), and final review/sign-off (the owner does that for now). A NOTE ON GROWTH. This is a prep-first role and we're hiring you to be excellent at prep. If you're ambitious and want to grow toward review work over time, there's genuinely room for that here. If you'd rather be the strongest preparer on the team and settle in for the long haul, that's just as welcome. No pressure either direction — tell us honestly where you sit. WHO YOU ARE You have 5+ years of US tax experience, with the bulk of it in hands-on preparation of complex returns — not bookkeeping, not entry-level data entry. Be ready to talk concretely about the returns you've prepared. You know S-corp work concretely: basis tracking, Section 199A computation, reasonable comp analysis, distributions vs. wages. Partnership and 1041 experience is a strong plus. You have hands-on experience with UltraTax CS, CCH Axcess, Lacerte, or ProConnect. You write in clear, professional English (C1 or higher). Your workpapers and planning memos need to be readable by a reviewer in one pass, and any client-facing notes need to land cleanly. You are detail-oriented and self-policing. When you don't know something, you say so and look it up rather than guessing. You flag your own uncertainty before someone has to ask. Your workpapers are organized enough that someone else can follow your reasoning without a phone call. You are comfortable with AI-augmented workflows. Our process uses Claude and TaxGPT alongside human judgment. Strong candidates are either already using AI tools in their work or genuinely curious to learn — we'll train you on ours. Candidates who view AI as a gimmick are not a fit. You are self-directed in a remote-first environment. The owner travels for portions of the year and time zone overlap will shift accordingly. We need someone who runs their own queue with minimal oversight. Real estate experience (rentals, short-term rentals, cost segregation, 1031 exchanges) is helpful but not required. We can teach the niche; we can't teach prep judgment. SOFTWARE STACK Required: UltraTax CS (preferred) or CCH Axcess, TaxDome, QuickBooks Online familiarity Acceptable in place of UltraTax: Lacerte or ProConnect with willingness to learn UltraTax Not acceptable: Drake-only experience Used in workflow: Claude, TaxGPT, IRS Solutions, Excel, Adobe Acrobat Pro If your tax software experience is Drake only, please don't apply. We're not the right fit. COMPENSATION Base salary: $3,000/month USD (paid twice monthly via Wise, on time, every time) 13th month: $3,000 paid in December, prorated for partial first year Internet stipend: $50/month Health allowance: $75/month Total annual comp: ~$40,500 USD Base may increase to $3,400/month for an exceptional candidate after the test process. Hours: Full-time, salary (not hourly, no overtime). This role follows the tax calendar, and the rhythm matters more than the raw hours. Filing season — roughly January 20 through April 15 — is the heavy stretch. Expect 50–55 hours with full Arizona overlap, and that time is focused return work. We pull back on admin, training, and process projects during the crunch so the prep gets done. Outside season, a standard week is around 40 hours, but it's a different mix — return work alongside admin, process improvement, and your own professional development, at a more sustainable pace. Summer is genuinely lighter. When the workload allows, we run reduced hours — often half-day Fridays, and during the slow stretch those shorter days don't require Arizona overlap at all. That's the firm's call based on what's in the queue, not a fixed schedule you can count on week to week. Light weeks don't cost you pay — you're salaried. Two short periods — late summer and early October, for extensions — return to a focused 40 with normal Arizona overlap. We give advance notice so you can plan around them. Time off: - All standard PH public holidays observed and paid. - A bank of 15 paid days/year (vacation + sick), yours to manage. - One long weekend (Friday–Sunday) off during tax season, scheduled with two weeks' notice. - Outside tax season, you manage your own time — take what you need from your bank, communicate, keep your work current. We don't micromanage the calendar. HIRING PROCESS 1. Application — Submit per the instructions below. Generic applications are discarded immediately. 2. First screen — 30-minute video call with the owner. 3. Paid prep test — One real client (sanitized data), $400 USD, ~2–3 hours, due within 7 days. You build the judgment-heavy workpapers in Excel and write a short prep memo — no tax software required. We're testing your prep judgment, not your software speed. 4. Judgment interview — a 45–60 minute call discussing your test, plus 2–3 scenario questions. 5. Reference check — One reference from a recent supervisor or peer. 6. Offer Total process: 2–3 weeks for serious candidates. HOW TO APPLY Send your application with the subject line: "Senior Preparer — [Your Full Name]" Include the following. If your application doesn't follow this structure, we'll assume you didn't read the post. (Strong, clearly-qualified resumes may still get a follow-up — but answering these up front moves you faster.) 1. Experience summary (3–5 sentences): Your years in US tax, how much is hands-on complex preparation, the type of firm you've worked at, and the volume/type of returns you've prepared. 2. Tax software: Which of UltraTax CS, CCH Axcess, Lacerte, ProConnect have you used? payroll, contractor payments, and 1099 tracking. * Experience supporting entrepreneurs, real estate businesses, SaaS companies, or multi-entity owners. * Experience with financial dashboards, spreadsheets, and operational reporting. * Strong Google Sheets or Excel skills. * Ability to use AI tools thoughtfully and responsibly in financial operations. ### Bonus Points * Experience with models, or automated reporting systems. ## Who You Are You are someone who: * Takes initiative instead of waiting to be chased. * Uses AI and automation to reduce repetitive manual work. * Thinks WHO WE ARE Functional Nutriments makes science-backed supplements for dogs. We're part of a small family of related businesses: a dog supplement company, an independent dog-health information site, a podcast network for dog lovers, and a publishing imprint. Our people (we think of ourselves as "Team Dog") are all fully remote professionals who live across several countries and time zones. We've operated this way for over twenty years. We're real and findable. (You're encouraged to look us up.) We treat the people who work with us like long-term partners. Some have been here for over a decade. If a step exists, you understand why it exists. We'll happily teach you our books; we can't teach you bookkeeping itself. Required: *  Solid working grasp of double-entry fundamentals (accrual basis, debits/credits, accruals, prepaids, the matching principle) *  At least 2 years of hands-on bookkeeping experience, including real QuickBooks Online work where you have owned the monthly books or close for at least one business (not just isolated data entry) *  Strong, clear written English — you'll communicate mostly in writing but video calls are a real thing within Team Dog *  Real attention to detail and the discipline to leave a clean audit trail *  Reliability and good async communication: you do what you say, and you flag problems early *  A quiet home work setup and stable internet and power Nice to have (not required): *  E-commerce bookkeeping experience (Shopify, Amazon, Stripe, PayPal, Wise) *  Experience with multiple entities or intercompany transactions *  QuickBooks ProAdvisor certification THE DETAILS *  Long-term independent contractor, fully remote *  About 20 hours/week to start, with genuine room to grow toward full-time *  USD$500-$700/month ($6 to $8/hour) depending on experience, with room to grow; paid twice per month via Wise *  Flexible schedule, with some overlap with U.S. Pacific/Hawaii hours for monthly close HOW TO APPLY — AND HOW WE HIRE We keep this simple and human: 1.  Apply here with your resume and a few sentences about your bookkeeping experience and why this role fits you. Include the word "ledger" in your note so we know you read the full post. Bonus points if you tell us about a special dog in your life. 2.  A short online skills screen (about 20 minutes, free). If your note and background look like a fit, we'll send you a personal message with a link to a quick, auto-graded screen covering bookkeeping fundamentals and QuickBooks — with a welcome video from our founder, so you know exactly who you're dealing with. 3.  A paid working interview. Our strongest candidates do a short, paid working session with us. PLUS you'll be compensated for your time as we walk through a real-world scenario and hear how you think. A real company, a real person on the other end, and we pay you for the practical stage. We're hiring one person and we intend to keep them for years. title: Business / Finance Controller (Remote)
description: WDM | E-commerce on Bol | Remote | 3–4 days per week (path to full-time as we grow) We're a Dutch e-commerce business selling on the Bol marketplace. We're small, we move fast, and we've automated a lot of the heavy lifting, including our P&L and cashflow, which now run on AI-driven models. So we're not looking for someone to put reports together. We already have the numbers. What we don't have yet is the person who looks at those numbers and d ---------- what we should actually do about them. That's the role. You'd work directly with me, the founder. When margin slips, you're the one who figures out why and what to change. When we're sitting on overstock, you're the one who d ---------- what to clear, at what price, and when, and backs it with the maths. When our models spit out a suggestion, you're the one who checks whether it's actually right before we act on it. What you'd own -Margin. Track it across products and channels, work out what's driving it up or down, and drive the changes that protect it. -Commercial decisions. Turn the data and the model output into real calls on pricing, promotions, assortment, and inventory. -Overstock. Treat it as a financial decision, not a guess. Put a number on it and d ---------- how and when to clear it. -A check on the models. Pressure-test what our AI finance tools produce before we trust it. The model proposes, you validate, I d ---------- . -SKU profitability. Find the winners and the quiet money-losers, and turn that into pricing and assortment decisions. The formal finance side. VAT, year-end, the accountant, compliance, and being in the room for any banking or financing conversations. -Cashflow. Keep an eye on the position, flag risks early, and understand how purchasing and stock decisions hit working capital. What it isn't A heads-up so we don't waste each other's time. This isn't a bookkeeping or monthly-reporting job, our systems already handle that. You also won't be building or fixing the data pipelines; we have a data analyst who owns data accuracy, and you'd work alongside them as an equal. Note: it might be that you spot these and work allong side the data analist to tackle bugs. Nobody's going to hand you a task list. You're the one making the calls. Who we're hoping to find The thing that's rare, and the thing we really want, is someone who has the Skills to equally handle P&L/Cashflow, can make SKU-level margin breakdowns, and can make decision messy stock data. Most finance people are only comfortable with the first; most data people only the last. We need someone who bridges all three. Example of decision comming from this -Pay of loans x amount of weeks -Push these products to gain turnover or lower overstock -Invest in these categories or when we are ready to invest in growth -Prep for Q4 financially and on SKU level. -Tips on lowering Opperational expenditure (where is the biggest cash leak and a step by step on how to fix it) Marketplace experience matters to us more than a long corporate finance CV. If you understand how fulfilment costs, returns, ad spend, and tied-up inventory eat into margin, you'll be of great impact from week one. We care more about how you think than how many years you've done it. A sharp person with three to five years and real commercial instinct beats someone with a longer history who's only ever produced reports. What we're really after is someone who's owned decisions, not just numbers, and who's comfortable telling me I'm wrong when the data says so. You'll need to be fluent in English, happy working remotely with a few hours of daily overlap with European time, and comfortable working with AI-driven finance tools and a modern e-commerce stack. What you get out of it -Real ownership from day one. You're not slotting into a process, you're shaping how we make decisions. -The finance and data side of the business is yours to lead. -A direct line to the founder. No layers, no politics. You bring the thinking, we d ---------- together, and you see your calls play out in the business fast. -Room to grow. This starts at 3–4 days a week and grows into a full-time leadership seat as we scale. Get this right and the role grows with the company. -A company that invests in you. We're built on quality, not just in our products and service, but in the life of our team. We back that up with a monthly health bonus you can put toward whatever keeps you well, gym, better sleep, whatever works for you. If we expect quality from you, we owe you the conditions to deliver it. -Remote, wherever you are, with just a few hours of daily overlap with European time. -USD $15–$20 an hour to start, with real room to move up as you prove yourself. How to apply Skip the long CV for now. Instead, I'd like a few things in your own words. First, tell me how you'd think about this: say we've got a chunk of capital tied up in overstock. How would you d ---------- what to clear, at what price, and when? I'm not after a perfect answer, you don't know our data yet, I just want to see how your mind works on it. Then share a quick story about a time you pushed back on a number, a model, or a boss, and how it played out. And tell me a little about what you've done before, and what made you want this role specifically. One last thing. We're after real A-players, and A-players like to work with other A-players. So if you've read this and thought yes, this is me, apply. I'm looking forward to reading it.

description: Majestix Collection is a premier destination for buying, selling, and trading luxury timepieces. We're looking for a detail-obsessed bookkeeper to accurately record every transaction that moves through our inventory — from the price we pay for a watch, through reconditioning and shipping, to the final sale and commission calculations. This is a role for someone who genuinely enjoys clean, accurate records and can follow a defined system without cutting corners. You'll be the single source of truth for our numbers, so precision and trustworthiness matter more than speed. What you'll do 1. Record what we pay for each watch Every watch enters through our Sell/Trade form, which automatically feeds into our MJX Sales Tracker (Google Sheets) under the "Submit and Shoot" tab. A thread is created for each watch in Zoho Cliq, where the amount paid is usually posted as a screenshot. You'll be tagged when a value is ready to record, and you'll log the purchase price in the correct row. 2. Record Shipping, reconditioning and parts costs When a watch is received and kept (not returned to the seller): Move its row from the "Submit and Shoot" tab into the "Stock and Sold" tab, placing it above the "Sold" section. Log the ship-in cost (we'll provide a rate sheet based on distance and insured value of the package). Log polish, service, and parts costs. Document what each cost is for using cell comments. When a single cost is made up of multiple components, use a formula (e.g. =value1+value2+value3) and describe each component in the cell comment. 3. Record the sale When a watch sells, the final numbers come from the platform invoice (eBay, Chrono24) or our own customer invoice — found in the sales thread (Zoho Cliq) or under Payments > Invoices. In the same row, record the initial amount we were paid. Record every fee involved in the sale — taxes, shipping, additional parts, platform fees, and so on. 4. title: Mid-Senior Bookkeeper (Multi-Entity)
description: We are looking for an experienced Mid-Senior Bookkeeper to manage and maintain the financial records across multiple related businesses. This is a responsible role requiring solid technical bookkeeping expertise, accuracy, and the ability to work independently with minimal supervision. We are not looking for a beginner; 5+ years of bookkeeping experience will be considered a strong asset. Our businesses operate across several different industries, which means you will be maintaining separate sets of books that are subject to different tax codes and regulatory treatment. You must be organized and disciplined enough to keep each entity's records distinct, accurate, and compliant, and comfortable learning the specific requirements of each business over time. The successful candidate will oversee full-cycle bookkeeping across multiple entities and ensure financial records are accurate, up to date, and properly maintained using QuickBooks Online and related systems. KEY RESPONSIBILITIES - Manage full-cycle bookkeeping across multiple business entities - Maintain accurate financial records in QuickBooks Online (QBO) - Keep books separate and compliant across entities with differing tax codes and industry regulations - Handle accounts payable and accounts receivable processes - Perform bank and account reconciliations - Generate and maintain financial reports - Support invoicing and payment tracking - Communicate with internal stakeholders regarding financial data and clarifications - Make AR/AP-related calls when necessary (vendors/customers for payment follow-ups) using our VOIP system - Ensure accuracy, compliance, and timely updates across all books REQUIREMENTS - Proven experience as a bookkeeper managing full-cycle accounts (not a beginner role; 5+ years of experience is a strong asset) - Strong expertise in QuickBooks Online (required) - Experience handling multiple business entities is highly preferred - Comfortable managing separate books across different tax codes and regulatory environments - Strong attention to detail and accuracy in financial data - Ability to work independently and manage responsibilities without micromanagement - Strong communication and reasoning skills - Comfortable making AR/AP-related calls when needed, using a VOIP system - Proficient in Microsoft 365 (Excel, Outlook, etc.) - Experience working in remote environments is an advantage TECHNICAL & HOME OFFICE REQUIREMENTS (PLEASE READ CAREFULLY) Reliable connectivity and power are critical for this role. You must have: - Redundant internet: a primary connection plus a backup (for example, a secondary provider or mobile hotspot). Internet interruptions cannot be allowed to stop your workday. - Backup power: a UPS for your equipment and/or generator access, so outages do not interrupt your work. - A capable computer: in your application, please state your computer's make/model and specifications (processor, RAM, operating system). - A quiet, professional workspace and a good-quality headset, since you'll be using a VOIP phone system for calls. COMPENSATION & GROWTH We are a group of growing companies with significant room to advance, including potential management opportunities, depending on performance. Starting wage is negotiated based on demonstrated competency, beginning on the conservative side of the range, with a wage review after an initial 3-month period and ongoing opportunities for raises, training budget, and equipment compensation as a long-term hire. Performance bonuses are available, based on: quality of work, quantity of work, being a team player, ownership thinking, productivity, reliability, initiative, and attention to detail. WHAT TO INCLUDE IN YOUR APPLICATION 1. A summary of your full-cycle bookkeeping experience, including total years and any experience managing books for multiple entities. 2. Your QuickBooks Online experience and any other accounting software you've used. 3. Your computer's make, model, and specifications (processor, RAM, OS). 4. Your internet setup, including your backup connection. 5. Your power backup arrangement (UPS, generator, etc.). INTERVIEW PROCESS Because this is a mid-senior, responsible role, shortlisted candidates should expect job-specific bookkeeping questions and a possible live screen-share session to assess hands-on competency in QuickBooks Online and reconciliations. We may also assign a short paid trial task as part of the process.
