title: Bookkeeper / Accounts
description: Long-term role with a family-run Queensland agribusiness Engagement Part-time to start (4 hrs/day), scaling to full-time for the right person Hours Some overlap with Australian Eastern Standard Time (AEST) preferred Reports to Business owner Software Xero (new file setup + ongoing) Start As soon as the right candidate is found About us We are a family-run agribusiness in rural Queensland, Australia, running several enterprises under one roof. Our main business is a paddock-to-plate meat operation selling Wagyu and premium beef direct to customers at markets and online. Alongside this we run cattle, produce hay, do contract farm work, and make a natural tallow-based skincare range. Because we have several income streams, we need someone who can keep our books clean and accurate, and show us clearly how each part of the business is performing. We are looking for one reliable, long-term person to take ownership of our bookkeeping and tax work so we can focus on running the farm. The role You will take over all of our day-to-day bookkeeping and tax-related work. The first big job is setting up a brand-new Xero file and moving us across from our current system. After that, you keep everything reconciled, GST-coded correctly, and ready for our Business Activity Statements (BAS) and end-of-year tax. Important: all BAS and tax documents are reviewed and signed off by the owner before lodgement. You prepare; we approve. What you will do • Set up a brand-new Xero file from scratch and manage the changeover from our current system — chart of accounts, opening balances, bank feeds and contacts. • Structure the accounts so each income stream (meat, cattle, hay, contract work, skincare) can be reported separately for both income and expenses — using Xero tracking categories. • Process and reconcile all bank transactions across multiple accounts. • Handle Australian GST correctly. Most of our food/meat sales are GST-free, while many of our supplier purchases include GST that we can claim back. You apply the right GST code to every transaction. • Prepare Business Activity Statements (BAS) and supporting tax documents for the owner to review and lodge. • Produce regular reports — profit & loss by enterprise, GST position and cash position — so we can see how each part of the business is tracking. • Maintain accurate records for end-of-year tax and liaise with our Australian accountant when needed. • Flag any errors, odd transactions or discrepancies early. We value someone who flags problems rather than hiding them. Must have • Solid hands-on experience setting up and running Xero (Xero certification / ProAdvisor is a strong plus). • Good understanding of GST and the difference between GST-free sales and GST-inclusive purchases — or a strong tax background and the ability to learn the Australian system quickly. • A bookkeeping or accounting qualification, with real experience keeping books for businesses. • Strong attention to detail and accuracy — this matters more to us than speed. • Reliable internet, your own computer, and good written English. • Honesty and discretion handling confidential financial information. Nice to have • Experience with Australian clients, BAS preparation, or the Australian tax system. • Experience with multi-enterprise, farming or primary-production accounts. • Confidence using Xero tracking categories for departmental / enterprise reporting. Why work with us • Long-term, stable role with room to grow your hours and responsibility. • Real ownership of the books — you run the system, not just data entry. • A friendly, straightforward team that values accuracy and clear communication. How to apply To apply, please send the following. Applications that answer the questions below will be prioritised — it tells us you read the ad and helps us find the right person quickly. 1. Your CV / resume. 2. A short note on your Xero experience and whether you are Xero-certified. 3. Your experience (if any) with Australian tax / GST / BAS. 4. Your hourly rate (in USD) and the hours per day you are available. Please also answer these three quick questions in your application: • In Xero, how would you set up the file so that income and expenses can be reported separately for several different parts of one business? (One or two sentences is fine.) • If a sale is GST-free but the supplier invoice for that product included GST, how do you treat each side in the books? • Have you prepared a BAS before, or worked with Australian GST? If not, how comfortable are you learning a new tax system? Shortlisted applicants will be asked to complete a short paid test task before we make an offer.

Our mission focuses on helping independent restaurants reclaim revenue from high-fee aggregators by giving them the tools to run their own high-margin delivery and catering channels. Our finance operations span multi-market driver pay, complex merchant payment reconciliation, and the high-level reporting discipline required to be investor-ready. We run lean, move fast, and value operational efficiency. Position Summary: Type: Full-time, 40 hours/week Location: Remote (Philippines) Hours: U.S. Business Hours (significant CST overlap required; exact schedule has flexibility, but core availability during peak U.S. morning/afternoon hours is necessary for team alignment). Reports to: Co-Founder / Chief Growth Officer (dotted line to CEO, Atlanta) Compensation: $13–$17/hr, commensurate with experience (FTE ~$27K–$35K/year) The Financial Controller is a hands-on role dedicated to owning the day-to-day accounting close and bringing extreme rigor to a high-transaction-volume, multi-market operation. This is an ownership seat for the books, reconciliations, and the strict controls required to keep them flawless. You will work directly with the founding team and have a highly visible impact on our Series A diligence readiness. Core Responsibilities 1. Financial Reporting & Month-End Close Full Close Ownership: Run the entire month-end close cycle, including journal entries, accruals, and GL reconciliation. Reporting Packages: Deliver a clean, accurate, and on-time monthly financial package. Diligence Support: Prepare financial schedules and reconciliations that feed directly into board reporting and investor diligence. 2. High-Volume Reconciliation & Spend Management Stripe / Payment Processing: Reconcile payments, refunds, and disputes across a growing merchant base (currently ~50 active merchants). Investigate and resolve all variances to zero. Driver Payroll: Tie out our multi-market driver pay infrastructure (hourly guarantees and catering workbooks) before payroll runs through Everee. Enforce a strict zero-variance tie-out prior to platform upload. Merchant Payouts: Reconcile merchant-level revenue, platform fees, and final payouts across all active markets; flag and resolve discrepancies immediately. Corporate Spend Ownership: Manage and optimize our Ramp spend management platform—overseeing corporate card workflows, expense auto-coding, receipt compliance, and bill pay mapping. 3. Treasury, AP/AR, & Internal Controls Cash Management: Maintain routine cash position reporting and assist the founders in tracking burn-rate metrics. AP/AR: Manage vendor invoicing, corporate expenses, and receivables tracking. Controls & Documentation: Build, maintain, and improve internal controls and process documentation to ensure the close process is repeatable and audit-ready. Process Automation: Document manual workflows and actively look for opportunities to make them AI-enabled or automated, ensuring that money-movement steps always require human approval. Candidate Qualifications Must-Have Requirements Experience: 3+ years in accounting/controller roles, ideally supporting a U.S.-based company. GL Ownership: Demonstrated experience running an entire month-end close cycle independently, not just supporting it. Software Proficiencies: Advanced, hands-on proficiency with QuickBooks Online (QBO), Ramp (or a closely comparable spend management / AP platform), and Advanced Excel (comfortable managing complex, multi-tab workbooks using advanced formulas, flags, and tie-out logic). Transaction Volume: Proven experience managing high-volume data reconciliation (e.g., payment processors, payroll platforms, or gig-economy settlement systems). AI Fluency: Actively leverages tools like ChatGPT, Claude, or similar to accelerate analysis, formula building, and reporting—while maintaining strong judgment around AI limitations and the need for human oversight on financial data. Communication: C1/C2 level English with exceptional written and verbal skills for seamless collaboration with a U.S. founding team. Infrastructure: A stable remote workspace with reliable internet and consistent availability for required U.S. CST overlap. Nice-to-Have Attributes Tech Stack Experience: Direct experience with Stripe, Everee (or similar payroll disbursement platforms), and Notion (where our core operational infrastructure lives). ERP & Scaling: Exposure to NetSuite or similar ERPs, helpful for future migration as the company scales. Automation Skills: Experience designing AI-assisted or automated workflows, prompt-driven reporting, or light scripting to eliminate manual close tasks. Industry Background: Prior experience in high-growth SaaS, marketplaces, gig-economy platforms, logistics, or restaurant technology. Benefits & Perks Performance Bonus: Eligibility for performance-based bonuses tied to milestones like successful close cycles, audit readiness, and process efficiency. Paid Time Off: Comprehensive PTO package aligned with observed US and PH holidays to ensure a balanced schedule. Professional Development: Dedicated annual budget for accounting certifications, advanced software training, or technical workshops. Schedule Flexibility: Enjoy some autonomy over your daily calendar, provided significant core CST collaboration hours are maintained. What Success Looks Like (First 90 Days) Day 30: Fully up to speed on the internal Stripe, Everee, Ramp, and driver-pay workbooks. Successfully shadowing and taking over weekly reconciliations. Day 60: Running the month-end close with minimal oversight and executing flawless, zero-variance driver pay tie-outs on every cycle. Day 90: Fully owning the close process independently, delivering the financial package strictly on the calendar, and having proposed at least two concrete process improvements to existing controls. description: Summary Chief Financial Officer (CFO) — Polar Haircare Location: Remote | Type: Full-time contractor | Compensation: $2,000 per month About Polar Haircare We're a fast-scaling direct-to-consumer haircare brand built around one breakout product: Instant Dye Shampoo — a 2-in-1 shampoo and gray-coverage dye that works in 10 minutes and lasts up to six weeks. Our customers are women aged 40–65 who are done with messy, damaging box dye and want something faster and cleaner. We sell across Shopify (DTC), Amazon FBA, Walmart and TikTok Shop, run meaningful paid media across Meta, Applovin and Google/YouTube, and operate a lean global team with a dual-warehouse (China + US) supply chain and a stack of specialist agencies. We're profitable, growing, and building the business with a potential acquisition in mind. The Role This is a hands-on, builder CFO — not a figurehead who manages a finance department. For a business our size, the CFO does the work: builds the models, closes the books with the bookkeeper, reconciles the vendors, runs the payments, and turns raw exports into decisions the founder can act on the same day. You will own every dollar that flows in and out of Polar Haircare. You'll know exactly where money is coming from and exactly where it's going — and you'll find the leaks before anyone has to ask. Your north star is structural margin: accurate unit economics, ruthless cost control, and reporting that makes the business easier to run and more valuable to sell. If you think in contribution margin, get uncomfortable when a number can't be traced to source, and enjoy finding the $40k/year nobody noticed was bleeding out — this is your role. What You'll Own Daily Close, Reporting & Performance -Own the daily financial close: prepare consolidated and channel-level P&Ls (Shopify, Amazon, TikTok Shop), including ad spend from every platform, all revenue streams, and operating expenses. -Deliver daily performance dashboards covering ROAS, MER, agency fees, indirect expenses, cashback, and the other levers that drive profitability — built for fast decisions. -Calculate and validate daily COGS on every item sold so margin reporting is always accurate. -Maintain weekly and monthly P&Ls for leadership with commentary on what moved and why. Unit Economics & Margin -Build and maintain landed COGS per unit and fully loaded cost per unit (product, freight, duties, packaging, pick/pack, last-mile). -Track gross, contribution, and net margin, and present a clean margin waterfall (Revenue ? Gross Profit ? Contribution ? EBITDA ? Net) at every reporting cycle. -Maintain channel-specific unit economics — especially Amazon (referral fees, FBA fees, storage, PPC) — never blended unless that's the point. -Set and recalibrate break-even and target ROAS as cost inputs change. Marketing & Agency Efficiency -Track total and channel-level ad spend, blended ROAS, MER, CAC, and CAC payback. -Measure each agency's fees as a % of the revenue or savings they manage and flag any that aren't earning their keep. -Surface the most and least efficient spend buckets and feed targets back to the media buyers. Cash Flow, Payments & Working Capital -Lead cash flow management and working-capital planning to keep operations liquid and funds working efficiently. -Run end-to-end payment execution for vendors, suppliers, employees, and subscriptions — on time, every time, no penalties or service interruptions. -Maintain optimal bank balances and manage credit-card funding, top-ups, and utilization. -Maximize credit-card cashback by tracking agreements and eligibility, and optimize banking/payment platform plans (Airwallex, Wise, etc.) against actual usage. -Deploy excess cash into short-term treasury options where it makes sense, within agreed risk limits. -Prepare bi-weekly cash flow reports highlighting inflows/outflows, runway, and key risks. Vendor & Inventory Control -Maintain real-time supplier ledgers: PO-wise commitments, payments made, and delivery status. -Run vendor reconciliations — verify balances, resolve discrepancies, and keep relationships and payables clean. -Maintain vendor registers and compliance documentation with key suppliers to support smooth operations and audits. -Perform periodic inventory valuation and flag slow-moving SKUs or overstock. Expense Governance & OpEx Control -Categorize every operating cost (payroll/contractors, software, agencies, fulfillment, processing fees, insurance, legal, misc.) and track OpEx as a % of revenue. -Own a live Subscription Master — every recurring charge, its owner, and its justification. -Produce periodic deep-dives (salaries, subscriptions, indirect expenses) with 3- and 6-month trend comparisons to surface savings and efficiency opportunities. Payroll & Bookkeeping Support -Execute payroll processing — accurate calculations, on-time disbursements. -Hand the bookkeeper/accountant complete documentation for accurate recording, timely reconciliations, and clean month-end closes (inventory, vendor balances, expense classification). Exit-Readiness & Strategic Support Our US accountant prepares the formal diligence/exit document pack. This role keeps the live operating picture that feeds it — so the story the books tell is accurate, current, and defensible. -Track SDE/EBITDA with clearly documented add-backs, plus trailing-12-month revenue, profit, and growth. -Monitor revenue concentration, repeat-purchase rate, LTV, and LTV:CAC. -Proactively flag "hair on the deal" — margin compression, single-supplier risk, revenue volatility, anything a buyer would question — before it surfaces in diligence. -Turn around ad-hoc, decision-critical analysis on short notice. What Success Looks Like -First 30 days: You can trace every line on the P&L to its source. You've found and documented where current reporting understates costs. -First 90 days: Daily/weekly/monthly reporting runs on a repeatable cadence with minimal manual effort. Accurate per-unit and per-channel economics are live, and break-even/target ROAS are set off real numbers. -First year: OpEx and agency spend are measurably tighter, cash flow is predictable, and the books are clean enough to drop into a data room without a scramble. Who You Are -Proven DTC / e-commerce finance experience — you've owned the numbers for a multi-channel consumer brand (Shopify + Amazon at minimum). -Fluent in the language of paid-media-driven brands: ROAS, MER, CAC, contribution margin, LTV, blended vs. channel-level economics. -Genuinely hands-on — you build the models and run the close yourself, not just review someone else's. -Elite with spreadsheets/financial modeling (Excel/Google Sheets); comfortable pulling and parsing raw exports (CSV/PDF) from Shopify, Amazon, banks, and ad platforms. -Rigorous about accuracy — you flag uncertainty, never present a shaky number as fact, and reconcile rather than defend. -Comfortable owning treasury, AP, payroll, and vendor management, not just FP&A. -Clear, direct communicator — you lead with the headline and the dollar impact, then show the math. Bonus Points -Experience preparing a business for sale / acquisition diligence. -Familiarity with multi-entity structures and cross-border operations/FX. -Working knowledge of accounting tools (QuickBooks/Xero) and banking platforms (Airwallex, Wise, Revolut). -Marketplace finance depth (Amazon FBA fee structures, TikTok Shop). In your application, tell us about a time you found a meaningful cost leak or margin opportunity in a business — what the number was, how you found it, and what changed. Looking forward to hearing from you!

title: E-commerce Bookkeeper (QuickBooks Online) — Multi-Platform Payout Reconciliation
job_title: E-commerce Bookkeeper (QuickBooks Online) — Multi-Platform Payout Reconciliation
description: E-commerce Bookkeeper (QuickBooks Online) — Multi-Platform Payout Reconciliation JOB TYPE: Full-time SALARY: $2,500/month LOCATION: Remote JOB DESCRIPTION: We're a US-based bookkeeping practice serving e-commerce and retail clients, and we're looking for a senior bookkeeper who already understands the part of this work that trips most people up: reconciling what a sales platform reports against what actually hits the bank. This is not a data-entry role. You'll own client books independently and review work done by others, so you need to genuinely understand why a payout never matches gross sales — fees, refunds, chargebacks, sales tax, held funds, and platform financing repayments that live in a separate report from the sales data. What you'll do: Own monthly close for multiple e-commerce clients in QuickBooks Online — categorization, reconciliation, and clean financials. Reconcile platform payouts to bank deposits, correctly separating gross sales, processing fees, refunds, and sales tax rather than booking the net deposit as revenue. Set up and maintain clearing accounts so sales, fees, and payouts flow correctly. Handle platform financing (e.g., Square Loans / Capital, Shopify Capital, PayPal Working Capital): book the funding as a liability, split repayments into principal vs. fee, and reconcile the liability against the platform's own loan/balance report each month. Account for cash sales, owner draws, and tender-type differences. Review junior bookkeepers' work and catch reconciliation errors before they reach the client. Required: 3+ years ecommerce bookkeeping, with strong QuickBooks Online expertise. Hands-on experience reconciling at least two of these: Square, Shopify, Stripe, Amazon, PayPal, Etsy. A real understanding of the payout-vs-sales gap and how to use a platform's reports to explain it. Strong written English and reliable overlap with US business hours (some hours between 9am–5pm Pacific Time). Accuracy, discretion with financial data, and the ability to work independently. Nice to have: Experience across several of the platforms above. Familiarity with platform financing products and how their repayments are reported. QuickBooks ProAdvisor certification. **Screening — to apply, complete all of these:** Send the following to our WhatsApp at ---------- : 1. Start your application with the word PAYOUT so we know you read this post in full. 2. Answer this in 3–5 sentences: A client's Square sales report shows $10,000 in gross sales for the month, but only $8,900 was deposited to their bank, and they have an active Square Loan. Walk us through what makes up that $1,100 difference and which report you'd pull to confirm the loan portion. 3. Your resume (PDF) 4. A 1–2 minute video introduction telling us about your e-commerce bookkeeping experience and which platforms you've reconciled. Applications without the keyword, a real answer to the question, and a WhatsApp submission (resume + video) will not be reviewed.

title: UK Construction - Finance Assistant
description: FINANCE ASSISTANT Smith & Sons Construction Services Ltd | Remote | Part-Time (25 hours per week) ABOUT SSCS Smith & Sons Construction Services Ltd (SSCS) is a premium residential construction company operating across East London, Havering and Essex. We are a director-led business building a strong, systems-driven foundation, and we are looking for an experienced finance professional to take ownership of our day-to-day finances as we grow. ABOUT THE ROLE We are looking for an experienced, UK-construction-literate virtual Finance Assistant to take ownership of our bookkeeping, reconciliation, reporting and supplier payments. The role begins by taking financial administration off the directors' desks. Over time - as you learn our systems and prove the core role can be done efficiently - it expands into higher-value finance work. We are looking for someone who can support the business for the long term, and the role is genuinely open to growing and being shaped around the right individual. The right person is meticulous, proactive and able to turn numbers into clear insight the directors can act on. This is a finance-first role, and the construction finance knowledge is non-negotiable. KEY RESPONSIBILITIES Bookkeeping and reconciliation (the core of the role) Own our dedicated accounts inbox and manage the working relationship with our external accounting and bookkeeping team - resolving their weekly queries and, more importantly, working to prevent those queries by keeping the books clean in the first place. Process all purchase invoices through Dext: ensure each is correctly tagged to the right project, the correct cost category is applied, and - critically - the correct VAT treatment is used, including the construction VAT domestic reverse charge where it applies. Stay alert to duplication. For example, where a director has photographed and uploaded an over-the-counter invoice that also arrives by email , verify the entry rather than relying solely on Dext and Xero's duplicate detection. Reconcile all company bank accounts and credit cards in Xero on an ongoing basis. Administer the Construction Industry Scheme (CIS): verify subcontractors, apply the correct deductions, and prepare and file the monthly CIS return through Xero. Reporting and insight Produce project-level reporting on all active jobs: total contract value against amount invoiced and amount remaining, cost-to-date split across labour, materials and subcontractors, and overall project profitability - in effect, cost-value reconciliation (CVR) and work-in-progress (WIP) tracking - flagging any cash flow risks early. Produce business-level reporting: regular profit and loss, cash position and forecasts, so the directors always know where the business stands. Treat cash flow forecasting as a distinct discipline, not just historical reporting. Deliver a structured update to the directors at least once a week in a scheduled video meeting, with shorter interim updates to a director by WhatsApp as needed. Client invoicing, credit control and supplier payments Manage client billing through Xero, including stage-payment and repeating-invoice schedules. PERSONAL ATTRIBUTES Proactive and self-managing - anticipates problems rather than waiting to be asked. Discreet and trustworthy with sensitive financial information. title: Bookkeeper — QuickBooks Online (Australian Tax & GST)
description: Cleanup, Restructure & Ongoing Bookkeeping  ·  Remote (Philippines) Long-term role with a family-run Queensland agribusiness Engagement Part-time, long-term — around 15-20 hours/week once established (more during the initial cleanup) Hours Flexible and deadline-based — we care that the work is done well and on time, not that you sit set hours each day Software QuickBooks Online (we are staying on QuickBooks — this is a QBO role) Reports to Business owner Start As soon as we find the right person About us We are a family-run agribusiness in rural Queensland, Australia, running several enterprises under one roof. Our main business is a paddock-to-plate meat operation selling premium Wagyu and grass-fed beef direct to customers at markets and online. Alongside this we run cattle, produce hay, do contract farm work, and make a natural tallow-based skincare range. We need one reliable, long-term person to take ownership of our bookkeeping so we can focus on running the business. The role We have used QuickBooks for many years and have a lot of history in the file. We are staying on QuickBooks — we are NOT migrating to Xero. The first big job is a thorough cleanup and restructure of our existing QuickBooks Online file so that each of our enterprises reports clearly and our GST is correct. After that, you keep everything reconciled, accurately coded, and ready for our Business Activity Statements (BAS) and end-of-year tax. Important: BAS and tax documents are prepared by you and reviewed/lodged by the owner. You prepare; we review and lodge. What you will do • Clean up and restructure our existing QuickBooks Online file — review the chart of accounts, remove duplicates, fix inconsistent coding, and set up a clean, consistent structure (you would confirm the proposed structure with us before making major changes). • Set up each enterprise to report separately (meat, cattle, hay, contract work, skincare) using QuickBooks Classes (and Locations where helpful), so we can see income and expenses for each part of the business. • Process and reconcile all bank and credit card transactions across multiple accounts. • Handle Australian GST correctly. Most of our food/meat sales are GST-free, while many of our supplier purchases include GST that we can claim. You apply the right GST code to every transaction, and review and correct existing coding during the cleanup. • Prepare Business Activity Statements (BAS) and supporting documents for the owner to review and lodge. • Produce regular reports — profit & loss by enterprise, GST position, and cash position — so we can see how each part of the business is tracking. • Flag any errors, unusual transactions, or anything without supporting documentation, rather than guessing. We value someone who asks and flags rather than assumes. Must have • Solid hands-on experience with QuickBooks Online — including cleaning up and restructuring an established file, not just data entry. (This is essential. Please only apply if you are genuinely experienced in QuickBooks Online.) • Good understanding of Australian GST, including the difference between GST-free sales and GST-inclusive purchases, and BAS preparation. • Experience using QuickBooks Classes (and Locations) for separating and reporting on different parts of a business. • A bookkeeping or accounting qualification, with real experience keeping books for businesses. • Strong attention to detail and accuracy — this matters more to us than speed. • Reliable, responsive, and able to work independently to deadlines. Good written English, reliable internet, and your own computer. • Honesty and discretion handling confidential financial information. Nice to have • Experience with Australian clients and Australian BAS/tax. • Experience with multi-enterprise, farming, or primary-production accounts. • Payroll / STP experience. Why work with us • Long-term, stable role with room to grow your hours and responsibility. • Real ownership of the books — you run the system, not just data entry. • Flexible, deadline-based hours — we trust you to manage your own time and deliver. How to apply Applications that answer the questions below will be prioritised — it shows us you read the ad and helps us find the right person quickly. Please send: 1. Your CV / resume (pasted into your reply or attached through OnlineJobs.ph please — not a Google Drive link). 2. A short note on your QuickBooks Online experience — in particular, any file cleanups or restructures you’ve done. 3. Your experience with Australian GST and BAS. 4. Your hourly rate (in USD) and the hours per day you are available. And please answer these three quick questions in your application: • In QuickBooks Online, how would you set up the file so that income and expenses can be reported separately for several different parts of one business? • If a sale is GST-free but the supplier invoice for that product included GST, how do you treat each side in the books? • If you took over a messy QuickBooks file with duplicate accounts and inconsistent coding, how would you approach cleaning it up? Shortlisted applicants will be asked to complete a short paid test task before we make an offer.

Within 90 days we want this hire owning the monthly close, producing clean GAAP-quality financial statements with management commentary, and serving as the day-to-day liaison with our external auditors at year-end. Day-to-day responsibilities Own the monthly close across three entities, hands-on. A representative slice of what this involves: bank reconciliations for cash, posting customer payments across credit card / PayPal / ACH channels, multi-state sales tax filings, full bank and credit card reconciliations, journal entries and accruals, intercompany allocations between US and Canadian entities, customer advance reclassifications, and AP/AR oversight. Manage the bookkeepers at each of the businesses, coach them on how to improve processes and identify technology to streamline processes. Prepare monthly three-statement financial packages (income statement, balance sheet, cash flow statement) with management commentary. Calculate quarterly bank covenant compliance against existing credit agreements (DSCR, leverage ratios, fixed charge coverage, working capital tests). Manage year-end external audit support across all three entities — prepare PBC schedules, respond to auditor requests, drive resolution of open items. It will take some time to understand the businesses and we would like to see the candidate embark to understand the 3 businesses and build a FAQ document of the people at the businesses, what their roles are and what you learn about the businesses. Then when there are slower periods in the role, we would like to see the creation of process documentation to professionalize our accounting processes. Must-haves CPA equivalent license required Experience having worked full time for an English speaking business in the past is required 6–12 years accounting experience, including ownership of monthly close Strong written and spoken English Multi-entity accounting experience QuickBooks Desktop and Sage 50 Canada experience is helpful, but not required US or Canadian SMB client experience preferred Comfortable preparing three-statement financial packages independently Hands-on orientation — "no task too small" Strong nice-to-haves Big 4 / SGV / SyCip background (audit experience preferred) Manufacturing or services industry experience Experience supporting acquisitions or year-end audits Work setup Fully remote with some Bridge overlap with USA Pacific Time. Weekly check-in call. After the transition period, we expect ad hoc calls outside of the designated hours to be uncommon — typically no more than 1–2 per week, often less. Email and Messages for everything else. Camera-on during calls. Ideal candidate profile The person who's right for this role is a mature senior accountant who takes pride in precision work and clean books. They've outgrown their current seat at a local firm or BPO client and want a longer-term home with a growing US business. They love a clean reconciliation. They write well in English. They're comfortable being the most senior accountant on the team but unbothered by hands-on detail work — they understand that a clean balance sheet doesn't reconcile itself. They are looking for a stable, dignified, longer-term role where their craft is valued and the work is interesting enough to grow into. Work Location: Remote

title: Finance & Accounting Coordinator
description: About the Role: New Beginnings Moving & Hauling is looking for a sharp, detail-driven part-time finance coordinator to keep the money side of the business clean and current — invoices out on time, receivables chased, books up to date, and a clear monthly picture for the owner. This is a focused, behind-the-scenes seat built for someone who lives in QuickBooks and catches the small errors before they become big ones. It is not a management or customer-facing role. Core Responsibilities: Same-day invoicing. Make sure an invoice goes out the same day every job is completed — no lag between work done and the customer being billed. Accounts receivable follow-up. Run a consistent past-due chase at 3, 7, and 14 days, escalating tone appropriately at each step and surfacing accounts that aren't responding. Expense tracking in QuickBooks. Enter and correctly categorize every expense so reports stay accurate and tax prep is painless. Payroll timesheet review. Check timesheets for discrepancies — missing punches, overlaps, unusual hours — and flag them. (This role reviews and flags; it does not process payroll directly.) Recurring billing & monthly summary. Bill recurring monthly contracts on schedule and prepare a simple monthly financial summary for the owner. Could Also Own (scope permitting within ~10 hrs/week): Bank & credit card reconciliation — match QuickBooks against statements monthly so the books are trustworthy. Fuel card reconciliation — match fuel card charges against the fleet log and receipts, and flag anything that doesn't line up (the company runs monthly fuel card audits — this role is a natural fit to support them). Tip payout reconciliation — verify the twice-weekly tip payouts match the jobs actually completed each work week. Accounts payable — track and schedule vendor and supplier bills so nothing goes late. Payment application & deposits — apply incoming customer payments to the right invoices and keep the deposit record clean. CPA / tax prep support — organize year-end documents, contractor 1099s, and sales-tax figures for handoff to the company's accountant. Light financial reporting — track simple health metrics like average days-to-pay (DSO) and an AR aging snapshot to include in the monthly summary. Ideal Candidate: Must have: Strong QuickBooks familiarity, genuine attention to detail, reliability with deadlines. Nice to have: Bookkeeping or small-business accounting background, comfort with spreadsheets, prior experience reconciling accounts. Not required: Management or customer-facing experience — the part-time scope is deliberately narrow.
